articles.title: Home Assistant swaps automation steps without rebuilding them
articles.dek: Replace keeps a step’s position and compatible settings, with one undo to restore it.
body: Home Assistant adds Replace to automation triggers, conditions and actions, and to script actions. Changing a light action from on to off no longer requires deleting it, adding a new step, moving it back and entering the target again.

The replacement keeps targets and options the new step accepts, along with its trigger identifier, enabled state and notes. Incompatible fields and the old name are dropped. One undo restores the original step exactly.
Blocks containing other steps are excluded, so replacing a step cannot silently discard an entire branch or loop.

pullRequests.title: Add Replace for automation triggers, conditions, and actions
Document replacing triggers, conditions, and actions in the automation editor

media.alt: An automation action menu with the Replace option highlighted.
media.caption: Replace keeps the step in its existing position.

articles.title: ESPHome sends microphone and line-in audio to Sendspin
articles.dek: Makers can turn an audio input into a source controlled by a compatible server.
body: ESPHome adds a Sendspin audio source for devices with a microphone or line input. A compatible server starts and stops capture, and the device sends the audio with its capture time so the server can align it with other audio.

The source accepts up to two channels at the microphone’s fixed sample rate and sends uncompressed audio. Makers can report whether audio is available through a sharing switch or sound-level measurement, and react when streaming starts or stops.

The availability signal guides automatic playback; it does not itself refuse a server’s request to start capture. This is an audio-input capability for ESPHome devices, beyond the computer capture tools previously covered.

[i2s_audio] Stamp microphone buffers with the DMA capture time
[sound_level] Allow more than one microphone channel

Require source clients to always report `signal`

articles.title: Home Assistant builds consumption totals from power and flow readings
articles.dek: Energy setup offers the missing calculated sensor instead of requiring it to be created separately.
body: Home Assistant lets owners add power-only devices, solar production and home meters to Energy by offering to create the missing energy sensor during setup. It can also reuse a sensor that already calculates the total from the same reading. A newly created sensor starts counting then; it does not reconstruct earlier usage.

The same setup works for gas and water sources and individual water devices that report a flow rate. The calculation follows the rate’s time unit, so a litres-per-minute reading produces a volume in litres.
Grid and battery setups need separate power readings for each direction. A single signed reading does not get the offer, because one calculation cannot separate the two directions.

pullRequests.title: Offer to create an energy sensor for power-only energy devices
Offer energy sensors from power for solar and home sources
Offer energy sensors from power for grid and battery sources
Offer gas and water sensors from flow rates

articles.title: Home Assistant stores backups in a self-hosted Seafile library
articles.dek: Each selected library becomes a backup destination, alongside file-count and storage readings.
body: Home Assistant adds Seafile as a backup destination for people running their own file-sync server. Each library has a Store backups option and a configurable backup folder, letting an owner choose which libraries receive backups.

The connection also reports library size, file count and last modification time. Sign-in exchanges the password for a device token rather than saving the password, supports a two-factor code when needed, and offers sign-in again if that token is revoked.
Chunked uploads and progress reporting accommodate proxies with upload-size limits, while downloads stream from the selected library.

Add reauth flow to Seafile
Add Seafile integration

articles.title: BookOrbit brings self-hosted audiobooks to Music Assistant
articles.dek: Listening positions stay in step between the audiobook server and the music player.
body: Music Assistant adds BookOrbit as a source for self-hosted audiobooks. Listeners can browse their libraries by author, narrator or series, search for a book and play it through Music Assistant while keeping their listening position synchronized in both directions.

The connection signs in to an existing BookOrbit server and brings its audiobooks, authors and narrators into the library. Its scope is audiobooks. This is justinwoodland’s first contribution to Music Assistant’s server.

pullRequests.title: Add BookOrbit audiobook music provider

articles.title: Home Assistant shares selected entities with voice assistants in bulk
articles.dek: Filtered table selections can be exposed or withdrawn together.
body: Home Assistant adds voice-assistant exposure controls to the entities table’s selection menu. An owner can filter by room, label or integration, select the matching entities, and expose them to an assistant without picking each entity separately in the voice settings.

The same menu stops exposing a selection and offers All assistants when more than one is available. Assistants configured manually in YAML are excluded, and only entities with a state can be selected for this operation.

pullRequests.title: Add bulk expose to voice assistants on the entities table

articles.title: Matter tilt-only blinds gain the right controls and state
articles.dek: Existing automations need tilt actions, and voice-assistant support changes with the correction.
body: Home Assistant represents Matter blinds that only tilt, such as the Aqara C100, as tilt controls instead of lift controls. Their state can follow the tilt position instead of remaining unknown, and the interface shows the matching buttons.

Automations and scripts using ordinary cover open, close, stop or toggle actions need the corresponding tilt actions. Opened and closed device triggers and conditions are no longer offered for these devices; state triggers and conditions remain the alternative.

The corrected representation also exposes existing limitations elsewhere: Assist open and close requests stop working, Google Assistant becomes query-only, and Alexa loses stop and on/off commands. Alexa open/close and HomeKit tilt control require tilt-position support. Covers that lift, including combined lift-and-tilt devices, are unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Fix state and buttons of tilt-only Matter covers

articles.title: Home Assistant lets owners drag controls across a picture
articles.dek: The card preview becomes an editing surface without triggering the controls themselves.
body: Home Assistant’s picture-elements editor lets owners click a control in the preview to edit it, then drag it into position. Dropping it writes the new position, instead of requiring repeated edits to percentage coordinates.

The preview suppresses the element’s normal action while editing. Dragging applies to elements positioned with percentage-based left and top values; an element covering more than half the picture must be selected first.

pullRequests.title: Select and drag picture elements in the card editor preview

articles.title: Music Assistant brings hidden library filters into view
articles.dek: The title bar shows active filters and puts sorting, search and view choices within reach.
body: Music Assistant’s library pages put search, sorting and filters beside the title and item count. Active filters are counted on the Filters button, making it easier to see why an album or artist is missing from the current view instead of hunting through the overflow menu.

The filter panel lists the active choices and offers Clear all, alongside searchable genre and album-type choices and music sources. The sort menu also switches between list and grid views; on a phone it opens from an icon. These changes apply to the eight main library pages, while detail-page listings retain their existing controls.

pullRequests.title: Show library sort, view and filters in the title bar

articles.title: ZHA repairs startup on two-slot ConBee and RaspBee radios
articles.dek: The Green Power addition exposed a firmware limit that could stop an existing network starting.
body: ZHA’s deCONZ radio library repairs startup on ConBee II and RaspBee II adapters after zigpy 2.4 added Green Power support. The firmware has room for two communication endpoints, while the new setup requested three; an adapter previously used by zigpy 2.1–2.3 could fail on every startup.

The library fits the endpoints together and retains ordinary home-automation traffic plus Green Power. On two-slot firmware this drops the legacy Zigbee Light Link endpoint, so incoming messages addressed to that endpoint are not received; outgoing traffic is unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Fit the Green Power endpoint into two-slot firmware

articles.title: ESPHome cameras prepare the light before taking a snapshot
articles.dek: A capture delay avoids sending the dark frame queued before a flash turns on.
body: ESPHome cameras gain a capture delay and start/end actions for single snapshots. A maker can switch on a light, wait for exposure to settle and then take the image, rather than receiving the frame that was queued before the light came on.

The delay can run for up to three seconds, and frames captured before it ends are discarded. The actions apply to single API and web requests, not continuous streams. On an AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM, a two-second delay produced consistent illuminated images instead of the nearly black first image after idle.

pullRequests.title: [esp32_camera] Add capture_delay and capture triggers for single images

articles.title: Home Assistant leaves new network-client trackers disabled
articles.dek: Existing trackers keep their state, while new ones receive clearer device names.
body: Home Assistant stops automatically enabling new network-client trackers just because another integration recognizes the same network address. New scanner trackers start disabled; existing trackers keep their enabled or disabled state.

In his contributor guide, Erik Montnémery explains that these trackers gain ordinary device information and names, avoiding doubled labels and trackers waiting for another integration to identify their device. UniFi’s own access points, switches and gateways remain enabled by default; its client trackers follow the new disabled default.

Owners who renamed a tracker may see its device name added as a prefix. Custom-integration authors also need to provide device information themselves before the compatibility fallback is removed in November 2028.

articles.title: ESPHome notices when a presence radar stops reporting
articles.dek: A disconnected LD2450 stops leaving a room falsely occupied indefinitely.
body: ESPHome detects when an LD2450 presence radar stops sending valid frames while the ESP device itself remains online. Live presence, target counts and positions become unknown instead of keeping the last reading indefinitely, and an optional connection sensor reports the loss.

The default timeout is five seconds. A powered, empty-room radar still sends frames, so an empty room does not look disconnected. The first valid frame restores the readings, while deliberate radar restarts receive a bounded grace period to avoid false alarms.

[ld2450] Document link loss detection

articles.title: Home Assistant reads electric-car telemetry from A Better Routeplanner
articles.dek: The connection brings an account’s vehicle garage into dashboards, without location tracking in this first step.
body: Home Assistant adds a connection to A Better Routeplanner that brings the vehicles in an account’s garage into Home Assistant. Readings include battery charge, range, power, voltage, battery temperature, charging state and odometer information.

The connection signs in through the service’s account authorization and receives telemetry from its cloud. This first implementation supplies sensors only; GPS tracking is a separate planned addition.

pullRequests.title: Add A Better Routeplanner integration

articles.title: ZHA quiets repeated reports from Tongou circuit breakers
articles.dek: Acknowledging the messages cuts needless Zigbee traffic without adding a misleading temperature sensor.
body: ZHA’s device library acknowledges temperature reports from a supported Tongou TO-Q-SY1-JZT breaker variant instead of discarding them. Without an acknowledgement, the breakers repeatedly resent the messages and crowded the Zigbee network.

On a test network with nine breakers and a CC2652P coordinator, incoming traffic fell from roughly 900 to 170 messages per minute. Existing controls and power readings remain; the reported temperature is deliberately not exposed because its value did not reliably follow the load. The change targets the tested variant and device layout.

pullRequests.title: Acknowledge temperature reports from Tongou TO-Q-SY1-JZT (_TZ3000_qeuvnohg)

articles.title: ZHA restores energy readings on Innr SP 240 plugs
articles.dek: SP 240 owners need a factory reset and fresh pairing to replace the old reporting setup.
body: ZHA’s device library restores room for energy, power, current and voltage reports on the Innr SP 240. The plug has only eight reporting slots, and settings with no useful role on this model could consume the space before the measurements were configured.

Existing SP 240 plugs retain their old reporting table. To benefit from the corrected setup, they need removal from ZHA, a factory reset and pairing again; Reconfigure alone does not free the occupied slots.

articles.title: ZHA tells dim-up and dim-down releases apart
articles.dek: Some Tuya automations need a second trigger to keep responding to either button.
body: ZHA’s device library tracks which dimming button was held before a remote sends its release command. This corrects reversed or missing release triggers on affected IKEA TRÅDFRI, RODRET and STYRBAR remotes and Tuya TS004F dimmer switches.

IKEA automations keep their existing trigger definitions. On the affected Tuya dimmers, an automation that used dim-down release to mean either button was released must also add the new dim-up release trigger. Raw stop events are unchanged.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps backups at the chosen time after clock changes
articles.dek: The schedule follows the configured time zone instead of a saved summer or winter offset.
body: Home Assistant corrects automatic backups running an hour early or late after a daylight-saving change. The schedule follows the configured time zone, rather than retaining the fixed offset saved with the last completed backup.
The earlier schedule could remain wrong until Home Assistant restarted. Tests cover both clock-change directions in Europe/Amsterdam.

pullRequests.title: Fix automatic backup time shifting by an hour after a DST change

articles.title: Home Assistant avoids stale dashboard files after an upgrade
articles.dek: The browser checks for the current page before falling back to its cached copy.
body: Home Assistant changes how its browser interface loads after an upgrade to prevent a blank screen caused by an old page pointing at deleted files. Navigation checks the network for the current page first and keeps the cached page as a fallback.

The cached interface can still open during proxy errors or while Home Assistant starts. A new version reloads the page once; a first installation does not. The initial network check can wait up to three seconds before falling back.

pullRequests.title: Fetch the index fresh on navigation and harden the service worker update flow

articles.title: ESPHome panels open password-protected remote dashboards
articles.dek: A rejected password stops retries before TightVNC locks out other viewers.
body: ESPHome’s remote-screen display gains password authentication, allowing panels to connect to VNC servers that require a password. It extends the remote dashboard viewer and touchscreen controls covered earlier this month.

A rejected password stops automatic retries and sets an error rather than repeatedly attempting the same login. Makers can explicitly reconnect after correcting the problem, or disconnect before putting a panel to sleep.

articles.title: Sendspin corrects silent and mistimed browser playback
articles.dek: Safari, Firefox and Android corrections target the JavaScript player, with Bluetooth limits on Apple devices.
body: Sendspin’s JavaScript player corrects several browser timing errors that could leave a browser silent or out of step with other speakers. On Android, implausibly large delay reports no longer cause every audio chunk to be discarded, and keeping the audio output open across disconnects avoids repeatedly introducing an extra delay.

Safari and Firefox receive separate timing corrections. In the contributor’s microphone measurements, an iPhone running iOS 18.7 with its built-in speaker moved from about 29 milliseconds early to 0.3 milliseconds early. On the tested MacBook Pro, Safari moved from about 70 milliseconds early to 5 milliseconds late. In Firefox on macOS, playback moved from about 22 milliseconds late to 0.3 milliseconds late.

These are corrections in the JavaScript client, not a claim about every Sendspin application. Apple Bluetooth and AirPlay outputs still need a manually chosen delay, and Android browser playback can remain late. Quick reconnects also stop carrying old audio into the new connection.

pullRequests.title: Fix late playback on Firefox
Fix playback offset on iOS and macOS Safari
Fix silent playback when the browser reports an implausible output latency
Keep the audio output across `disconnect()` and add `destroy()`
Fix playback timing after delay changes, clears and reconnects

articles.title: Linux Voice Assistant shortens its wake-sound delay
articles.dek: Using PulseAudio by default reduces a long-idle playback delay on a tested Raspberry Pi.
body: Linux Voice Assistant uses the PulseAudio output by default rather than letting its audio player choose a driver. On a tested Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, that reduces the wait for a wake sound after the assistant has been quiet for a long time.

In Florian Asche’s tests, the measured interval from opening the wake-sound file to finishing it was about 2.3–2.4 seconds with the previous automatic output after five or thirteen hours of silence, compared with 0.87 seconds on PulseAudio after about nineteen hours. The few runs used a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, Satellite1 HAT, Docker and PipeWire’s PulseAudio compatibility service; they do not establish the same improvement on other hardware.

Explicit device choices stay unchanged. The new default requires a reachable PulseAudio service, including PipeWire’s compatible service, and does not fall back to another audio driver if it is missing.

pullRequests.title: Default the audio output device to pulse
Document how audio input and output reach the host

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps a speaker’s identity across restarts
articles.dek: Stale device records stop replacing its settings and Home Assistant entity on every startup.
body: Music Assistant preserves a speaker’s existing player identity when an old native-device record claims its audio connection but never comes online. Previously, the speaker could be recreated with a new identifier on each restart, losing its settings and its Home Assistant entity.

The existing player is restored first. A native device can take over later only after it registers and accepts the connection. Speakers wrapped around a disabled native device remain playable until that native device is enabled again.

pullRequests.title: Keep a Universal Player's id when a stale native player claims its protocol
